name: @mgcrea/mcp-google-search-console

tools.name: gsc_auth_status
tools.description: Whether the server is configured and signed in, which Google account the token belongs to (the account decides which properties exist at all), how many properties it can read, the granted scopes, whether the write tools are registered, and the quota model. When unconfigured, returns the exact setup steps. Call this first when a tool you expected is missing, a property is not found, or a setting seems to have no effect (`config_issues` lists values that were clamped or ignored).

tools.name: gsc_auth_login
tools.description: Sign in with Google: opens the consent screen in the browser and waits for it to finish, then stores a refresh token (mode 600) and reports the signed-in account. Pick the Google account that has access to the Search Console properties you want — the account, not any argument, decides which properties are readable. The app is unverified, so Google shows a warning first: Advanced → Go to (app). If no browser can be opened, or the wait runs out, returns the authorize URL instead and keeps listening for 5 minutes; call gsc_auth_status afterwards. Logging in again replaces the stored login.

open.description: Open the consent screen in the default browser. false only returns the URL.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the consent to complete before returning the URL instead. Defaults to 120.

tools.name: gsc_auth_logout
tools.description: Revoke the stored refresh token at Google and delete it locally. Recoverable by calling gsc_auth_login again.
